name: Kalter Schlag
description: Kalter Schlag (Cold Stroke) is a traditional trick-taking game from Hamburg, Germany, closely related to the 'Ramsch' variants of Skat. Played with 32 cards by four players, it is an 'avoidance' game where the objective is to earn as few points as possible. The name refers to the sudden loss that can occur when a player's hand 'cools' or a surprise mistake leads to a massive point capture.

history.origins: Developed as a social variant of Skat and Schafkopf in Northern Germany. It is specifically identified with the pub culture of Hamburg and the surrounding regions.
timeline: 19th Century: Ramsch-style games grow out of a frustration with traditional bidding.
Early 20th Century: Kalter Schlag standardizes in the Hamburg region.
Present: A niche but dedicated community keeps the game alive in North German card clubs.
history.cultural: Commonly played for small stakes where the local loser is the 'Cake' or pays for the round of drinks.
history.evolution: The game's scoring (points are bad) reversed the traditional goal of trick-taking, leading to a much more cautious and defensive playing style.

setup.deck: 32 cards (7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each suit).

rules.objective: Avoid taking tricks containing high-value cards. The first player to accumulate 2,000 points loses the entire session.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit. If unable, must play a trump (Jack) if held.
2. Highest Jack wins; if no Jack, highest card of led suit wins.
3. **Kontra/Re**: Before playing the first card, players can 'double' the value of the round points.
keyRules: Jacks are permanent trumps. Ranking: Clubs (High) > Spades > Hearts > Diamonds (Low).
Must follow suit; if unable, must play a trump Jack if held
Only the player who takes the MOST points in a round receives those points as penalty
Durchmarsch (winning all 8 tricks): Scorer gets 0, others take 120-point penalty

strategy.basic: Dump your Aces and Tens on tricks that OTHER players win. The goal is to stay 'under' the point threshold of the biggest loser of the round.
strategy.intermediate: Duck Tricks: Even if you could win a trick, sometimes it's better to play a low 7 or 8 to ensure you aren't forced to lead the next trick (which is always dangerous).
strategy.advanced: The Durchmarsch Gambit: If you hold 3+ Jacks and several Aces, you might try to win every single trick. This is high risk; if you miss even one trick, you will likely end up with the most points and take the penalty.
tips: Jacks are only 2 points but they 'pull' other cards. Use them to force opponents to play their Aces.
The 'Kalter Schlag' (surprise loss) usually happens in the 6th or 7th trick when a player is 'squeezed' into winning a 20+ point trick.
